reason: Under the Flexible Retrieval minimum storage duration question the quote states a minimum of 90 days and a pro-rated charge for the remaining days when deleted, overwritten or transitioned earlier; claim and display match.
The quote states restore notifications send an S3 Event Notification when an object has restored from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and the temporary copy is available; display is verbatim.
The quote states the retrieval request creates a temporary copy in S3 Standard while leaving the archived data intact, and that you specify the number of days the copy is kept.

The quote limits the 1-5 minute Expedited figure to all but the largest objects (250MB+) and says Standard and Bulk times are typical; the claim drops the 250MB+ exception and the word typically for Standard and Bulk, and the condition field is empty.
The quote states up to 10% lower cost than S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval for archive data accessed 1-2 times per year and retrieved asynchronously; both displays are in the quote.

The quote makes the free data transfer out conditional on moving all data off AWS in accordance with the process below (a request process); the claim keeps eligible and all data but drops the process condition, so it reads as automatic.
The quote states a single general purpose bucket can contain objects across all storage classes except S3 Express One Zone and that general purpose buckets are recommended for most use cases.

The packet context is cut off before the quote; via show on www/s3/faqs line 480 the sentence follows the description of the three Glacier classes (Instant, Flexible, Deep Archive), so all these storage classes includes every S3 Glacier class and states multi-AZ redundancy within a Region.
Under the question about changing from S3 Standard-IA to S3 Standard with COPY, the quote names an S3 Standard COPY request charge and an S3 Standard-IA data retrieval charge.
The quote states 99.9% availability, the same as S3 Standard-IA, and service credits if availability is less than 99% in any billing cycle.
The quote states S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval has a minimum object storage charge of 128KB.
The quote states a minimum of 90 days of storage and a pro-rated charge for remaining days for objects deleted, overwritten or transitioned before 90 days.

The quote states no Restore request is needed unlike Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive; the preceding sentence in the same answer gives the same milliseconds latency and high throughput as S3 Standard and S3 Standard-IA.
The quote states it is ideal for data rarely accessed (once a quarter) that requires milliseconds retrieval, with a lower storage price and slightly higher data access costs than S3 Standard-IA.
The quote ties changing, unpredictable or unknown access patterns to S3 Intelligent-Tiering being the default storage class; display verbatim.
The quote states a Restore request is needed and objects move to Frequent Access in 3-5 hours from Archive Access and within 12 hours from Deep Archive Access.

The quote states that once the asynchronous archive tiers are enabled, objects not accessed for a minimum of 90 days move to Archive Access (up to 71%) and after 180 days to Deep Archive Access (up to 95%).
The quote states 99.9% availability and 99.999999999% durability and the same low latency and high throughput as S3 Standard.

The quote allows One Zone-IA as a target only from the Frequent, Infrequent and Archive Instant Access tiers; from the optional archive tiers only Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive are allowed; the claim drops these per-tier conditions and implies any object can go to One Zone-IA.
The quote states charges for monthly storage, requests and data transfer plus a small monthly monitoring and automation charge per object.
The quote states an object in the Infrequent Access or Archive Instant Access tier that is accessed later is automatically moved back to Frequent Access.
The quote states the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class has no minimum storage duration.
The quote states there are no retrieval charges in S3 Intelligent-Tiering and no additional tiering or lifecycle charges when objects move between its access tiers.
The quote states no minimum billable object size, objects smaller than 128KB not eligible for auto-tiering, always charged at Frequent Access rates with no monitoring and automation charge.
The quote states 30 consecutive days to Infrequent Access (up to 40%) and after 90 consecutive days of no access to Archive Instant Access (up to 68%).
The quote gives the example rule archiving logs/ to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval 30 days from creation and expiring after 365 days; the claim keeps it as an example.
The quote states S3 Lifecycle policies apply to both existing and new S3 objects.
The quote states uncommitted parts are still charged and the policy removes incomplete multipart uploads and the associated storage after a predefined number of days.
The quote states you can specify the policy at the prefix or at the bucket level.
The quote states no additional cost to set up and apply Lifecycle policies and a transition request charged per object when it becomes eligible for transition.

The quote states expiration by object age and multipart upload expiration by upload age; the preceding sentence in the same answer gives transitions by age from S3 Standard to Standard-IA, One Zone-IA and the Glacier classes.
The quote states Macie uses machine learning to recognize sensitive data such as PII or intellectual property and gives visibility into where it is stored; the context places this data in Amazon S3.

The quote requires account credentials plus a valid six-digit code and serial number from the authentication device; the claim text drops the serial number (only the display keeps it), so the claim understates the second factor.
The quote states S3 stores data redundantly across a minimum of 3 Availability Zones by default; claim keeps the by-default qualifier.
The quote states active-active or active-passive configuration and, in active-passive, failover controls shift request traffic to the chosen alternate Region and account within minutes.
The quote states up to 60% acceleration for data sets replicated across Regions and, based on AWS Global Accelerator, routing over the AWS network to the lowest latency copy.
The quote states the underlying buckets can be Requester Pays and the requester pays request and data transfer cost of both the bucket and the Multi-Region Access Point.
The quote states for objects larger than 100 MB customers should consider multipart upload; the claim keeps should consider.
The quote states you pay only for what you use and there is no minimum charge.
The quote states Object Lock protection is maintained regardless of storage class and throughout S3 Lifecycle transitions between storage classes.
